KEY MESSAGE 1...Low clouds continue to move in this morning,
lasting into Tuesday night. Rain showers possible heading into 
Tuesday night, as well as early this morning.

Low clouds have continued to descend across southern New England 
from the north as a backdoor front pushes in from the north. 
Some patchy drizzle remains possible this morning, particularly 
closer to the MA/NH/VT border. Latest HREF guidance indicates 
the possibility for two rounds of showers across the region 
today: one round later this morning, then another this evening 
heading into early tonight. Latest guidance has shown that these
may extend a bit more south into SE MA, including the Cape and 
Islands this evening. Low pressure associated with a shortwave 
moving across northern New England is the primary driver for the
later showers, which could lead to them becoming more robust 
towards northern MA. 

Notably, lows Tuesday night will be a bit warmer following this 
disturbance as the flow shifts more SW and 925 mb temperatures 
climb to nearly 18C overnight. Lows will likely only be in the 
50s to low 60s ahead of quite a warm day for Wednesday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Isolated shower possible Wednesday, but drier 
overall. Dry conditions return Thursday with seasonably cool 
temperatures.

The low centered over northern New England continues tracking
off to the northeast and surface high pressure with upper 
level ridging begins to build in over SNE behind it. With the 
continued westerly winds, downslope flow with the aforementioned
elevated low level temperatures (~18C at 925 mb) and good 
mixing with the boundary layer will all combine to support a 
much warmer fall day. Highs will likely climb into the 70s, with
some areas even approaching 80. Based on the latest ensemble 
probabilities, the highest temperatures are most likely towards 
the CT Valley and in much of the coastal plain of SE MA, where 
highs are expected to reach well into the upper 70s. With the 
westerly downsloping flow, gusts around 25 mph are not out of 
the question, especially for the higher elevations Wednesday 
afternoon.

Isolated showers remain a possibility Wednesday given the
trailing cold front associated with the disturbance to our 
north and PWATs remaining quite elevated. Latest CAMs have a 
signal for some of these showers towards the afternoon towards 
eastern MA and RI. Guidance generally has PWAT values between 
1.0-1.25" Wednesday, drying out considerably heading into 
Wednesday night and Thursday with high pressure and a drier 
airmass over eastern Ontario continuing to build east. 925 mb 
temperatures Wednesday night drop drastically compared to the 
afternoon, falling to below 10C and generally remaining there 
through Thursday. This will be supportive of lows dipping back 
into the 40s and 50s with daytime highs Thursday in the 60s. 
With high pressure in full force Thursday, expect drier and more
seasonably cool conditions.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain
Friday into early Saturday. Gusty NW winds and below normal 
temperatures expected to be left in its wake.

A deeper, more potent shortwave is expected to deepen well into
the Great Lakes region heading into Friday morning and continue 
tracking east into the northeastern US Friday into Saturday. 
Latest guidance indicates a LLJ from the SW may set up over the 
region in conjunction with an anomalous moisture plume of PWATs 
up to around 1.5" Friday, which given this environment is quite 
favorable for widespread rain. However, instability is quite 
lacking across the guidance, so heavier downpours aren't as 
favored. Ensemble totals for this event range between 0.30" to 
around 0.75", with the Canadian and the ECMWF ensembles favoring
the wetter solutions for southern New England. Given the time 
out from this system, more refined timing details are a bit 
uncertain at this time, but the general idea across the guidance
is that rain moves in sometime Friday morning and moves out 
Saturday morning.

Following this rainfall, a strong cold front is expected to push 
through the region Saturday morning, kicking off strong cold air
advection underneath more cyclonic flow. Latest guidance even 
has the 540dam line extending south into southern New England as
925 mb temperatures sink below 0C Saturday. PWATs fall below 
0.25" as this dry, cold air sets in. Lows Friday night fall into
the 40s and upper 30s, with the higher elevations likely 
falling below to at freezing. Highs Saturday may struggle to 
reach the low 50s across the interior and lows Saturday night 
will likely dip below freezing across the region, with the 
exceptions being areas closest to the coasts and urban areas. In
the midst of this colder air, strong NW winds prevail, with 
gusts to 45 mph becoming a possibility given the steeper lapse 
rates and tight gradient between the exiting strong low and high
pressure situated well to our SW.
